steps.text: Check response: Shake shoulders and shout 'Are you okay?'
If no response, tilt head back and lift chin to open airway.
Check breathing: Look, listen, and feel for normal breathing for 10 seconds.
If NOT breathing normally, call emergency services immediately.
Start CPR: Place hands in center of chest. Push hard and fast (100-120 beats/min, 2 inches deep).
Apply direct pressure to the wound using a clean cloth or hands.
Maintain pressure constantly. Do NOT remove the cloth if it soaks through; add more layers.
If bleeding is from a limb, elevate it above the heart if possible.
If bleeding doesn't stop, apply a tourniquet 2-3 inches above the wound (not on a joint).
Ensure the person is breathing normally.
Place them in the Recovery Position: roll them onto their side, support head, bend top leg.
Monitor breathing constantly until help arrives.
Do NOT move the injured person unless they are in immediate danger.
Immobilize the injured area. Use a splint if trained, otherwise keep it supported.
Apply a cold pack wrapped in cloth to reduce swelling.
